'''James Taft "Jimmer" Fredette'''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.namecandy.com/celebrity-baby-names/blog/2010/12/15/these-basketball-players-have-uncommon-skills-and-names |title=These Basketball Players Have Uncommon Skills and Names |publisher=NameCandy |date=2010-12-15 |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Eric |last=Medved |url=http://blog.timesunion.com/medved/jimmer-goes-a-long-way-in-repeating-his-amazing-2009-performance-against-zona/1392/ |title=Jimmer goes a long way in repeating his amazing 2009 performance against ‘Zona |newspaper=Albany Times Union |date=2010-12-12 |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref> (born February 25, 1989) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player who gained national fame during his college career at [[Brigham Young University]]. In 2011, he was the leading scorer in [[NCAA]] Division I basketball, and earned several [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|National Player of the Year]] honors, including the [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden Award]],<ref name="SN">[http://www.byucougars.com/Filing.jsp?ID=15358 BYU Men's Basketball Information Zone]. BYUCougars.com (2011-03-22). Retrieved on 2011-06-09.</ref> the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]],<ref name="NABC-Naismith"/> the [[Adolph Rupp Trophy]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sltrib.com/sltrib/blogsbyusports/51530926-65/fredette-player-award-wooden.html.csp |title=BYU's Jimmer Fredette wins Adolph Rupp Award, makes Wooden All-America team |author=Jay Drew |date=March 30, 2011 |work= |publisher=''[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]'' |accessdate=1 April 2011}}</ref> and the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2011/oscar110328.html |title=BYU's Fredette Wins 2010–11 Oscar Robertson Trophy |author= |date=March 28, 2011 |work= |publisher=[[USBWA]] |accessdate=1 April 2011}}</ref>  Fredette is a native of [[Glens Falls, New York]].<ref name=Layden/>

==Early life==
Fredette was born February 25, 1989, in [[Glens Falls, New York]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jimmer_Fredette/Summary/9263 |title=Jimmer Fredette |author= |date= |work= |publisher=RealGM |accessdate=3 March 2011}}</ref> to Al and Kay Fredette, the youngest of three children.<ref name=Layden>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/tim_layden/03/18/byu/index.html |title=With a crowd behind him, Fredette hoping to take BYU to new heights |first=Tim |last=Layden |publisher=''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' |date=March 18, 2009 |accessdate=January 26, 2011}}</ref> Named James Taft, Fredette later received the nickname "Jimmer" from his mother.

From his early childhood, he showed unusual dedication to athletics, his older brother TJ recalling, "He was the most determined, competitive four-year-old I had ever seen." TJ, an aspiring [[hip hop music|rapper]], helped train him for his basketball career since before kindergarten.<ref>{{cite web|last=King |first=Jason |url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news?slug=jn-byu031810 |title=Oh, brother, BYU survives |publisher=RRivals.com |date= |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref> He regularly played with TJ, seven years older, and TJ's friends on the family's backyard court. Fredette was able to hit [[three-point field goal|three-pointers]] at age 5, and developed moves to get around his larger opponents. TJ also remembered that his brother "willed himself to find ways to win, even if he was physically outmatched. From the time he was 10, I was telling everybody he was going to make the NBA."<ref name=Anderson2>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1181209/2/index.htm |title=A Real Jimmer Dandy |first=Kelli |last=Anderson |publisher=''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' |page=2 |date=January 31, 2011 |accessdate=January 29, 2011}}</ref>

Other family members assisted Fredette in his development. His father, a financial adviser, introduced Jimmer to schoolyard competition against adults at age 8. As Jimmer developed, his father took him on occasional road trips to [[Hartford, Connecticut|Hartford]] and [[New York City]] for more intense competition, and also helped to coach his AAU teams. His mother allowed him to bounce basketballs throughout the house, and even built a dribbling studio for him in their basement. Her brother Lee Taft, a personal trainer who now operates a speed training school in [[Indianapolis]], started him on running drills as a 5-year-old, and still works with Fredette.<ref name=Anderson2/>

Jimmer also has an older sister, Lindsay, [[Miss Teen USA 1998|Miss Teen New York 1998]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://issuu.com/thechronicle/docs/chronicle_jimmer |title=Section 2: Jimmer Fredette Chronicle |newspaper=The Chronicle |location=Glens Falls, New York |page=3 |date=December 2–8, 2010 |accessdate=January 26, 2011}}</ref> Fredette's father became a [[The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints|Mormon]] at the age of 18 after meeting [[Missionary (LDS Church)|missionary]] Kimball Rogers—the father of Fredette's BYU teammate Stephen Rogers<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/700102377/BYU-basketball-reunites-Fredette-Rogers-families.html | title=BYU basketball reunites Fredette, Rogers families | accessdate=February 27, 2011 | author=Swensen, Jason | date=2011-01-20 | publisher=Deseret News}}</ref>—while his mother is a [[Catholic Church|Catholic]]. Fredette, along with his two older siblings, chose to become Mormons after their parents allowed them to choose their religion.<ref name=Layden/>

==High school career==
Fredette was ranked among the nation's top 75 shooting guards by ESPN.com in high school.  He is Section II and Glens Falls High School's all-time leading scorer, ranking 6th on New York's all-time scoring list, with 2,404 points.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bronstein |first=Jonah |url=http://niagara-gazette.com/sports/x982166564/BYU-star-Jimmer-Fredette-comes-to-UB |title=BYU star Jimmer Fredette comes to UB |publisher=Niagara Gazette |date=December 29, 2010 |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref>  Fredette was named first-team all-state by the New York State Sportswriters Association and the ''[[Times Union (Albany)|Times Union]]'' as a junior and senior.  He had several memorable on court moments in his career at Glens Falls, including 12 different 40 point performances in his senior season,{{cn|date=April 2011}} and a shot against Voorheesville High School in the season opener of his junior year in which he banked a three pointer off the glass and in with his opposite hand to force overtime at the end of regulation{{cn|date=April 2011}}. In his senior season Fredette led his team to a 25–2 record and the Class A State Championship game which they lost to a [[Peekskill High School]] team led by current [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse University]] forward [[Mookie Jones]].  He played AAU for the Albany City Rocks alongside current [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State University]] point guard [[Talor Battle]].<ref>{{cite news |accessdate=2010-11-17 |url=http://www.nytimes.com/slideshow/2010/03/16/sports/ncaabasketball/20100316-NCAA_4.html |title=Defining the Great Midmajor Player  |work=New York Times |date=2010-03-16}}</ref> Fredette averaged 25 points per game to help the Rocks to a third-place win over the Minnesota Magic at the 2006 AAU National Championships.<ref name=byucougars_profile>{{cite web|url=http://www.byucougars.com/Profile.jsp?ID=3062 |title=BYU Men's Basketball Athlete Profile (Jimmer Fredette) |publisher=BYUCougars.com |date= |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref> He also lit up the Sportsfest Tournament at Cedar Beach in Allentown, PA during a prestigious outdoor summer tournament. His performance included four three-pointers in the first half of the championship game fighting against 10–15 mph gusts of wind. {{Citation needed|date=February 2011}}

Despite his high school accolades, he went largely unnoticed by the traditional "basketball powers".<ref name=Anderson2/> He received offers from 12 schools<ref name="Rec">{{cite web |url=http://www.heraldextra.com/sports/college/byu/basketball/article_9f04220e-b44d-51f2-936b-f3cdba071f8b.html |title=A look back: Jimmer finds way to BYU with a big assist from a Syracuse coach  |author=Jason Franchuk |date=December 5, 2010 |work= |publisher=''[[Daily Herald (Utah)|The Daily Herald]]'' |accessdate=26 February 2011}}</ref> and ultimately chose to attend BYU,<ref name="Rec"/> which was sister Lindsay's alma mater and the flagship school of the LDS Church.<ref name=Anderson2/>

==College career==

===Freshman year===
Fredette played in all 35 games for the Cougars as a true freshman, helping BYU earn a 27–8 record and capture the Mountain West Conference Championship. He averaged 18.5 minutes, 7.0 points, 1.7 assists and 1.1 rebounds per game and was the team's fifth-leading scorer.<ref name=byucougars_profile/>

===Sophomore year===
{{seealso|2008–09 BYU Cougars men's basketball team}}
Fredette played in all 33 games of his sophomore season starting 32 of them.  He was second on the team in scoring (16.2), three-point shooting percentage (.382), three-point makes (52) and free throw percentage (.847) and first in steals (1.5) and assists (4.1).  He scored in double figures 29 times and had 20-plus points 8 times. Fredette led the team in scoring 10 times and assists 19 times and was named first team all Mountain West.<ref name=byucougars_profile/> Fredette became BYU's first point guard to earn first-team all-conference honors since Marty Haws in 1990.

===Junior year===
{{seealso|2009–10 BYU Cougars men's basketball team}}
On December 28, 2009, Jimmer Fredette scored 49 points against the Arizona Wildcats, setting a new BYU record and a new McKale Center record for points scored in a single game.<ref>{{cite web|last=Leung |first=Diamond |url=http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/878/fredette-for-49 |title=Fredette for 49 |publisher=ESPN |date= |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref>

On March 11, 2010, Fredette scored 45 points, shooting 10-for-23 from the field, and making 23-of-24 free throws, in his team's 95–85 win over TCU. His scoring broke the Mountain West Conference tournament and tournament single-game records. His free throw shooting broke the MWC tournament record for free throws in a single game.<ref>{{cite web|last=Leung |first=Diamond |url=http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/6069/jimmer-fredette-with-another-record-breaking-night |title=Another record-breaking night for Fredette |publisher=ESPN |date= |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref>

On March 18, 2010, Fredette helped secure BYU's first round win in the NCAA tournament. He went on to score 37 points and hit two 3-pointers in double-overtime to seal the Cougars' 99–92 win over 10th-seeded Florida, the first time they had reached the second round of the tournament in 17 years.  In doing so, he tied a BYU record for most points scored in an NCAA tournament game. ([[Danny Ainge]], 1981) .<ref>{{cite web |accessdate=2010-11-17 |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300770252 |title=Fredette sinks key 3-pointers as No. 7 BYU knocks out No. 10 Florida in 2OT  |work=ESPN.com |date=2010-03-18}}</ref>

Fredette considered foregoing his senior year and entering the draft after his junior year, and he was expected to be picked 25th to 30th, but in the end he decided to stay at BYU and play his senior year.

===Senior year===
{{seealso|2010–11 BYU Cougars men's basketball team}}
Fredette was named co-captain of his team alongside [[Jackson Emery]] and Logan Magnusson.<ref name=byucougars>{{cite web|url=http://www.byucougars.com/Filing.jsp?ID=14410 |title=Captains Announced for 2010–11 |publisher=BYU Men's Basketball Press Release |date=2010-09-24 |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref> He was the top-ranked point guard in the nation according to [[Rivals.com]]<ref>{{cite web |accessdate=2011-02-02 |url= http://collegebasketball.rivals.com/viewcbse.asp |title= College Basketball Power Rankings |work=rivals.com |date=2011-02-02}}</ref> and led the nation in points per game despite frequently being double- or triple-teamed, which allowed him to open up shots for his teammates.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ksl.com/?sid=14552641&nid=272 |title=BYU X's & O's: Double-Team |publisher=ksl.com |date=2011-02-27 |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref>

Fredette scored a season-high 47 points in BYU's road victory over [[Utah–BYU rivalry|archrival]] [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]] on January 11, 2011, scoring 32 in the first half including a 40-foot buzzer beater to end the first half. He finished with 16–28 on shooting along with 4 rebounds and 6 assists. He also scored 39 against [[2010–11 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|UNLV]] on January 5, 2011 and 33 in a rematch against the same [[University of Arizona]] team he scored 49 against his junior season. On December 8, 2010, he returned to his hometown of Glens Falls to play [[2010–11 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]] in the [[Glens Falls Civic Center]], scoring 26 and attracting a crowd of 6,300, nearly half of Glens Falls' population of 14,354.

On January 26, 2011, in the Mountain West Conference's first battle of top-10 teams, which attracted a crowd of over 22,700 at [[BYU]]'s [[Marriott Center]], Jimmer scored 43 points against previously undefeated [[2010–11 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]], ending the game in a 71–58 victory. This was his third game this season to score over 40 points. When BYU played on the road in San Diego, BYU dealt SDSU its only other loss that season, with an 80–67 victory in which Fredette had 25 points, 9 assists and 3 rebounds.

He became the Mountain West Conference's all-time leading scorer on Feb. 5, 2011 with a 29-point performance versus UNLV in the Marriott Center.

On March 7, 2011, Fredette was named both the Mountain West Conference's player of the year and the CBSSports.com National Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/14788241/national-awards-jimmer-clear-choice-as-top-player |title=National awards: Jimmer clear choice as top player |publisher=CBSSports.com |date=2011-03-08 |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref>

On March 11, 2011, in the semifinals of the Mountain West Conference Championship Tournament, Fredette broke BYU's career scoring record, passing [[Danny Ainge]], and set the school's single game scoring record with a career-high 52 point game against [[2010–11 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team |New Mexico]], to whom BYU had lost twice in the regular season. He also set BYU's record for most points in one half by scoring 33 points in the first half of the game.<ref>{{cite news|last=Drew |first=Jay |url=http://www.sltrib.com/sltrib/cougars/51416210-88/points-byu-cougars-fredette.html.csp |title=Jimmer Fredette’s 52 points carry BYU past New Mexico |publisher=The Salt Lake Tribune |date=2011-03-11 |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref>

On March 17, 2011, Fredette led 3rd-seeded BYU's scoring in the first round of the NCAA tournament with 32 points, leading the Cougars to a 74–66 victory over 14th-seeded Wofford, and the second consecutive year BYU would advance to the second round of the NCAA tournament.<ref>{{cite news|last=Griffin |first=Andrew |url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705368922/BYU-basketball-Jimmer-Fredette-turned-it-on-when-BYU-needed-it-most.html |title=Jimmer Fredette turned it on when BYU needed it most |publisher=''Deseret News'' |date=2011-03-17 |accessdate=2011-03-19}}</ref>

On March 19, 2011, Fredette again led BYU's scoring with 34 points as they defeated 11th-seeded Gonzaga 89–67, and advanced to the third round of the NCAA Tournament ([[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship |Sweet Sixteen]]) for the first time since 1981, falling to the Florida Gators in a rematch of the game from last year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310780252 |title=Jimmer Fredette's 34 puts BYU in school's first Sweet 16 since 1981, but Fredette and BYU would fall short as they lost to the Florida Gators in over time 83–74 (Fredette had 32 points in his last game with BYU). |publisher=ESPN |date=2011-03-19 |accessdate=2011-03-20}}</ref>

He was picked to the First Team All-America by [[Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711|title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams|work=[[Fox Sports]]||publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media|date=Mar 7, 2011|accessdate=June 21, 2011}}</ref>

For his senior year performance, Fredette was nigh unanimously named the 2011 national player of the year, being so named by the [[Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year|Associated Press]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=6280416 |title=Jimmer Fredette is AP player of year |author= |date= |work= |publisher= |accessdate=1 April 2011}}</ref> ''[[Basketball Times]]'',<ref name="Basketball Times POY">{{cite news|url=http://www.byucougars.com/Filing.jsp?ID=15356 |title=Basketball Times |agency=Associated Press |date=April 1, 2011 |work= |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=21 March 2011}}</ref> [[CBSSports.com]],<ref name="deseretnews.com">{{cite news|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705368321/BYU-basketball-Jimmer-Fredette-is-SIcoms-national-player-of-the-year.html |title=BYU basketball: Jimmer Fredette is SI.com's national player of the year |newspaper=Deseret News |date=2011-03-09 |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref> the [[NABC Player of the Year|National Association of Basketball Coaches]],<ref name="NABC-Naismith">{{cite web |url=http://www.sltrib.com/sltrib/cougars/51556842-88/award-fredette-player-nabc.html.csp |title=Jimmer Fredette wins 2011 Naismith Award and NABC award |author=Jay Drew |date=April 3, 2011 |work= |publisher=''[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]'' |accessdate=4 April 2011}}</ref> [[SI.com]],<ref name="deseretnews.com"/> Athlon Sports,<ref>[http://www.athlonsports.com/columns/national-notebook/jimmer-gets-nod-player-year Jimmer Gets Nod as Player of the Year]. AthlonSports (2011-03-07). Retrieved on 2011-06-09.</ref> and ''[[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|Sporting News]]''.

[[File:Fredette at Walmart.jpg|thumb|right|Display in an [[Orem, Utah]], [[Walmart]] promoting "Jimmermania"]]
After BYU's nationally televised game against [[San Diego State University|San Diego State]] in which Fredette scored 43 points, the media attention around Jimmer became significant. Fredette gained "pop culture lore,"<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ksl.com/index.php?nid=272&sid=14159382 |title=BYU's Fredette gaining pop culture lore |author=Matt Hopkins |date=January 27, 2011 |work= |publisher=[[KSL]] |accessdate=13 March 2011}}</ref> and his name became a verb—opponents on whom he scored large amounts of points were considered "Jimmered."<ref name="CNN">{{cite news |url=http://www.cnn.com/2011/US/03/13/college.basketball.jimmered/index.html?hpt=T2 |title=With March Madness, 'Jimmermania' may reach fever pitch |author=Michael Yount |date=March 13, 2011 |work= |publisher=CNN |accessdate=13 March 2011}}</ref> His image appeared in on one of the regional covers for [[Sports Illustrated]] for the 2011 NCAA tournament preview issue.<ref name="TourneySI" />

[[YouTube]] became replete with highlight reels and tribute songs about Fredette (e.g., "Teach Me How to Jimmer");<ref name="CNN"/> and in February 2011 BYU student Michelle Peralta, who chastised people for "worshiping" Jimmer via the campus newspaper and [[Facebook]], was inundated by comments from hundreds of Fredette supporters, the popular media declaring that "Michelle Peralta got Jimmered."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dreamcatchermedia.com/jimmered |title=Michelle Peralta got Jimmered |publisher=Dreamcatchermedia.com |date= |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref> 

While revealing his NCAA Tournament Brackets, President [[Barack Obama]] said of Fredette: "Unbelievable. Best scorer obviously in the country. Great talent."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ksl.com/?nid=272&sid=14751208 |title=Obama heaps praise on BYU's Jimmer Fredette |publisher=ksl.com |date= |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref>

==Playing style and personality==
In a January 2011 article, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' writer Kelli Anderson said about Fredette's playing style,
{{cquote|Facing the opposition's best defender (or, more often, defenders), he pulls up going right or going left. He shoots off the dribble, off the wrong foot, off balance, off the glass. He finishes in traffic with a dozen deft moves, including a funky scoop shot, originating from his waist, that he can make with either hand.<ref name=Anderson1>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1181209/index.htm |title=A Real Jimmer Dandy |first=Kelli |last=Anderson |publisher=''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' |page=1 |date=January 31, 2011 |accessdate=January 29, 2011}}</ref>}}

He has even been noted by several collegiate and NBA players across the country. [[Kevin Durant]] of the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] posted on his [[Twitter]] account that "Jimmer Fredette is the greatest scorer in the world!!",<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.newsok.com/thunderrumblings/2011/01/28/kevin-durant-marvels-at-jimmer-fredette/ |title=Kevin Durant marvels at Jimmer Fredette |publisher=Thunder Rumblings |date=2011-01-28 |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref> while [[Steve Nash]] of the [[Phoenix Suns]] tweeted "Jimmer Fredette? Man, that name's straight outta Hoosiers. No wonder he never misses...".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://twitter.com/SteveNash/status/31075282408443904 |title=Steve Nash: Jimmer Fredette? Man, that |publisher=Twitter |date= |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref> [[Jared Sullinger]], a forward at [[Ohio State University]], said "Yooo Jimmer is going off right now. Pure scorer."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://twitter.com/Jared_Sully0/status/30480863779102720 |title=Jared Sullinger: Yooo Jimmer is going off r |publisher=Twitter |date= |accessdate=2011-03-17}}</ref>

Other facets of his personality have been noted by other college coaches. Former Utah coach [[Jim Boylen]] has cited "swagger and confidence" as Fredette's biggest weapons, and [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova's]] [[Jay Wright (coach)|Jay Wright]] has also remarked favorably on Fredette's on-court aggressiveness, comparing him to [[Pete Maravich]] in that respect. However, according to Anderson, Fredette "is fiercely competitive while remaining unassuming and likable," noting that [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] coach [[Sean Miller]] hugged Fredette after he scored 49 on the Wildcats, and the Utah fans who saw Fredette score 47 on the Utes in January 2011 gave him an ovation as he left the court.<ref name=Anderson1/>

Jimmer describes his older brother TJ as his biggest fan and supporter. TJ, whose song "Amazing" was written for his brother, said, "I see him play, and it gives me chills sometimes when he hits some of those big shots and the crowd is going crazy."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ksl.com/?nid=148&sid=14151663 |title=TJ Fredette talks about growing up with Jimmer |date=January 26, 2011 |author=Keith McCord |publisher=[[KSL-TV|KSL]]}}</ref>

In an article published in Sports Illustrated, Marcus Morris, a forward at KU, noted the work ethic and moral character Fredette exhibited while at USA Basketball camp. Said he, "He’s got heart. You can see he has a feel for the game, and he can SHOOT IT from anywhere. Even if you try to box-and-one the guy, he brings it up and just pulls up from the hashmark. That’s tough to guard."<ref name="TourneySI">[http://tourney.si.com/2011/03/16/cover-kids-marcus-morris-talks-jimmer/ NCAA Tournament – Luke Winn – SI.com » Posts Cover Kids: Marcus Morris Talks Jimmer «]. Tourney.si.com (2011-03-16). Retrieved on 2011-06-09.</ref>

An unusual set of Fredette fans reside in the [[Mount McGregor Correctional Facility]], a medium security prison, where he and his older brother played games with the inmates.
